# 29_prepare_big_ingest.sh - Hand a too-big deposit over to the big ingest

<!-- BEGIN pipeline-callers: generated by tools/automation_doc_links.py, do not edit by hand -->
:::{attention} Usually run by a Bitbucket pipeline
`29_prepare_big_ingest.sh` is normally not run on its own. The Bitbucket pipelines listed below call it as one step of a longer job, after earlier steps have prepared its inputs and environment. Run it by hand mainly for debugging or local testing.

**Called from [bitbucket-pipelines.yml](https://github.com/AEADataEditor/replication-template/blob/master/bitbucket-pipelines.yml):**

## Description

Run by the "Check downloads" step of the regular ingest pipeline when the deposit ZIP did not fit into the cache. It

1. checks whether the recorded size (ZIP + unzipped contents + overhead, see [](#help-big_ingest)) is above `bigingest_threshold_mb` in `config.yml`; if so it sets the big pipeline's VM to `4x` in `bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, commits (through `20_commit_code.sh`) and pushes;
2. posts a Jira comment (through `70_publish_comment.sh`) that the regular pipeline aborted because the deposit is too big.

The pipeline then triggers the big ingest with the `atlassian/trigger-pipeline` pipe, whether or not the VM was changed, and fails the regular pipeline.

## Usage

```bash
./automations/29_prepare_big_ingest.sh <regular-pipeline-name> <big-pipeline-name>
```

### Requirements

The pipe triggers the big ingest as the shared system user (the AEA System User), not as whoever started the regular pipeline, so it works the same for every user. It reads two variables:

- `BITBUCKET_TRIGGER_EMAIL`: the system user's Atlassian account email (passed to the pipe as `ATLASSIAN_ACCOUNT_EMAIL`).
- `BITBUCKET_TRIGGER_TOKEN`: an Atlassian API token for that account (passed as `ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN`). The account must have write access to the repositories, and the token must be allowed to call the Bitbucket API.

**Checking whether they are set.** In Bitbucket, go to *Workspace settings → Pipelines → Workspace variables* (shared by all repositories in the workspace), and also *Repository settings → Pipelines → Repository variables*. Look for both names. Secured variables show only their name, never the value, so being listed means it is set. A repository variable overrides a workspace variable of the same name.

**Creating them.** If they are missing, add both as workspace variables, marking the token *secured*. If they are missing or the token is not accepted, the pipe fails with an authentication error: the regular pipeline still fails, but the big ingest is not started.
